x: Lacey) Tony Fairclough, one of Britain's leading juniors, fights his way past Graham (Windsor) in the Southern championships to finish 3rd. Two weeks later he was 5th in the 'National'.

Left on his own for some time he probably felt in the latter stages that he would at least salvage second place, but the field had closed up alarmingly behind and in the last mile or so Barratt, Heaver, Franklin, and Briault all swept past with Badgery, Presland and Graham close behind.

Easily the best of the remainder was Graham, whilst Carl was showing young Colin what its' all about (he slept through the proceedings). John was in good form and soon appeared and it was not long before Ray came in to give us another team win.
Graham, Martin and Andy showed the sort of backing which could give them a place medal in the Southern and possibly the National Junior races when Matt and Justin Chaston come into the team.
